raw_response.assistant_text:
Here's how the two paths compare across the dimensions that matter most for your Series A goal.

Capital and runway
£750k buys you roughly 18-24 months of runway depending on burn, giving you time to miss a quarter and recover. £250k extends your current 8 months to perhaps 12-14, leaving almost no margin for error on the path to £50k MRR.

Growth capacity
At 10% month-on-month, you reach £50k MRR in about 17 months from £18k. That means £250k almost certainly cannot get you there within 12 months without a step-change in growth rate. £750k lets you hire ahead of the curve and potentially accelerate that trajectory.

Dilution
£750k at a typical pre-seed valuation costs you 15-25% equity. £250k costs roughly 5-10%. That dilution difference compounds: less equity now means more leverage at Series A and beyond.

Investor signal
A larger raise signals conviction and gives you a stronger negotiating position with Series A investors. A lean raise can signal capital efficiency, but only if you hit the metrics. If you miss, it signals the opposite.

Execution risk
£250k concentrates all risk on hitting the MRR target perfectly. One bad month, one key hire falling through, one churn spike, and you are fundraising from a position of weakness. £750k distributes that risk across a longer window.

The core tension: £750k gives you the best chance of hitting Series A metrics, but costs more equity now. £250k preserves equity but makes the 12-month target very difficult to hit without everything going right.

Your model already captures most of this structure. The missing piece is a cost or burn rate factor, which would sharpen the runway comparison considerably. Want me to add that, or run the analysis first to see where the model currently points?
